recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. It directly implements the Published clarification in the active datatype source without touching diagrams or unrelated datatype semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-20853 was a Published/Persuasive MnM clarification request for FHIR-core datatypes. It asked whether primitive datatype subtypes such as markdown/string or url/uri can be substituted for one another, and the resolution said the specification should clarify that data types cannot be substituted with subtypes.
initial_application: Git history shows an initial R5 application in ec83d5b505, which added a source/datatypes.html note saying 'Subtypes cannot be substitued for datatypes'. The commit did not mention FHIR-20853 and the note was removed the next day by b9fd58139d during unrelated RatioRange datatype work, so the current page had only the older uri/url/canonical-specific note.
additional_context: FHIR-9168 records the same false-impression problem around profiled/specialized datatypes, and FHIR-40555 later refined string-to-markdown compatibility wording by distinguishing single-type elements from choice elements whose wire names include the type. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record. source/fhir.ini maps datatypes to datatypes.html by default, confirming the edited source is in build scope.
reconciliation: Added one bullet to the primitive datatype notes in source/datatypes.html stating that datatype specialization does not imply substitutability, that instances are valid against explicitly allowed datatypes, and that a choice element allowing string does not also allow markdown unless markdown is explicitly listed.
source_changes: source/datatypes.html: added a primitive datatype notes bullet clarifying that specialized datatypes are not automatically substitutable unless explicitly listed by the element definition.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue documenting that profiled/specialized datatype presentation falsely implied markdown could substitute for string.
Later Published issue refining string-to-markdown compatibility language, supporting the choice-element example in this fix.
